name: Communitarianism
summary: Communitarianism holds that people are shaped by the families, communities and traditions they belong to, so a good society balances individual rights with duties to others and the common good. It criticises liberal individualism and unregulated markets for eroding community, and places civil society (family, schools, local groups) between the individual and the state. The responsive form associated with Etzioni is centrist and pluralist, combining social conservatism on family and moral education with openness to state-backed social rights.
scope: Mainly responsive communitarianism of Amitai Etzioni and the 1990 Responsive Communitarian Platform, together with the philosophical communitarian critics of Rawls (Sandel, Taylor, MacIntyre, Walzer) as described in the SEP. It excludes authoritarian communitarianism (Asian-values style) as a separate strand, and many answers on issues the movement never addressed (immigration, trade, guns aside, sexuality) are low-confidence inferences or splits.

keyFigures.name: Amitai Etzioni
keyFigures.role: Founder of responsive communitarianism and the Communitarian Network.

keyFigures.name: Michael Sandel
keyFigures.role: Philosopher whose critique of Rawls's unencumbered self shaped the communitarian debate.

keyFigures.name: Alasdair MacIntyre

sources.author: Christian Science Monitor, 1993 (and Education Week, 1991)

sources.title: Amitai Etzioni
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Etzioni's balance of rights and common good, privacy and security, markets and global governance (page flagged as edited by its subject).

universal-healthcare.rationale: Supporters back positive rights such as subsidised health care and social security, though the platform gives little detailed economic policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the concern that unregulated markets erode families and communities and from support for work valued and fairly rewarded.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Communitarians say unregulated capitalism undermines families and local communities, and Etzioni rejects pure utility-maximising, though they do not favour planning either.

public-ownership.rationale: Communitarians favour local ownership and civil-society bodies over either state or market, and do not set out a view on nationalising utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Etzioni's worry is concentrated private economic power distorting politics, but no tax programme is stated and adherents range from centrist to conservative.

unions-good.rationale: Workplace and intermediate bodies are valued as communities, and Sandel cites Brandeis on industrial democracy, but unions are not a stated platform plank.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rights are held to depend on community and may be limited for significant common-good gains (Etzioni), so property is not near-absolute; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The critique of unchecked capitalism and of corporate power distorting government supports tighter limits, e.g. on large chains and plant closings.

cut-welfare.rationale: The welfare state is criticised for displacing civil-society obligations, but supporters also back social security and subsidised services, so wholesale cuts are not the line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Industrial democracy and local ownership are cited approvingly, but collective worker ownership of firms is not a defining demand.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Etzioni's The Limits of Privacy and Patriot Act writings accept security measures like airport screening and testing where the common good justifies limiting privacy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The platform supports drug testing in public-safety jobs and a moral order stressing responsibility over licence; legalisation is not part of it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: A review reports Etzioni answering hate speech with more speech rather than censorship, though communitarians stress shared norms; contested.

strong-leader.rationale: The platform wants strong, participatory, responsive democracy and an informed public that can resist demagogues.

state-harmful.rationale: Communitarians hold that community and civil society need an active government and rest on it; the state is to empower communities, not vanish.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform calls for domestic disarmament and reads the Second Amendment as community militias, not individual gun slingers.

empower-police-military.rationale: Sobriety checkpoints and screening are backed, but no call for more police or military funding is stated.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the stress on shared moral norms and family responsibility over individual choice.

decide-locally.rationale: The platform says what can be done locally should not pass to state or federal level, with exceptions for urgent national problems like the environment.

rehabilitation.rationale: Punishment is not a developed communitarian topic; adherents emphasise both moral order and responsibility, so split.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is the prototypical community and the first line of moral education; the platform favours two-parent families but a new familism with both parents involved, not simple restoration.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by the platform; adherents divide between traditionalist and responsive strands.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not a stated communitarian position; the movement spans Catholic social conservatives and secular liberals such as Etzioni.

more-religion-public.rationale: Churches are valued as civil-society institutions, but Etzioni and Galston prefer secular approaches and schools teach shared values to avoid religious indoctrination.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-discrimination is endorsed but programmes of corrective action are not stated; inferred split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; though selves are held to be socially constituted, this is not applied to gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nations are described as communities of memory worth sustaining through service and history teaching.

gradual-change.rationale: Major policy changes need serious social challenges to justify them (Etzioni) and traditions are respected though critically evaluated.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not addressed in the main sources; the nationalist strand might favour limits while the responsive strand rejects particularism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Etzioni calls for global governance resting on national representation, and the platform hopes for an eventual global community, but strengthening the UN is not central.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; communitarians worry about community disruption from markets but have no trade doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Etzioni wants a muscular but moral foreign policy and global governance, so adherents are split on putting national interest first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Etzioni's Security First advocates a muscular moral foreign policy; inferred for the wider movement.

open-borders.rationale: Community membership and bounded communities of memory make open borders unlikely; not directly addressed.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the platform allows for national action on environmental degradation but takes no stand on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental degradation is named as a problem needing national or international action; the degree is inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Moral and social renewal, not technology, is the communitarian remedy; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No communitarian view on nuclear power exists.

revolution-justified.rationale: Reform through strong democracy and a social movement akin to the Progressive movement is the stated route.

experts-over-public.rationale: Strong, participatory democracy and an informed public are emphasised over rule by experts.

central-planning.rationale: Communitarians put civil society above both state and market and want government to empower, not direct, communities.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism is not discussed; local ownership and industrial democracy are cited favourably but not required.

land-value-tax.rationale: No communitarian view on land taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Duties and reciprocity are stressed (people owe something back for benefits), which cuts against unconditional payments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Concern for local communities may favour protection, but no trade stance is stated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Intermediate bodies and local communities rather than the state are to lead; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Local ownership is praised but wide small property is not a stated principle.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Work and saving are honoured in the platform and no communitarian source proposes abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; communitarians are not libertarian monetarists.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Intermediate bodies are valued, but state-recognised wage and price setting is not a communitarian programme.

one-party-rule.rationale: Communitarians want open participation and strong democracy; the authoritarian strand is distinguished from responsive communitarianism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; democratic participation is the stated ideal.

democracy-best.rationale: Strong democracy is the platform's aim, though the stress on informed publics and moral culture qualifies the clause about voters choosing badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Participation is prized but direct legislation is not stated; deliberation is stressed.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power is to remain in representative democratic government, with civil society beneath it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Multinational states must protect minority rights; secession is not endorsed in the sources.

natural-rulers.rationale: Communitarians reject hierarchy and rigid stratification in the responsive strand and favour open participation.

political-violence-never.rationale: The platform emphasises peaceful conflict resolution, though never-justified absolutism is not stated.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not stated; the platform stresses peaceful conflict resolution and tolerance.

separate-church-state.rationale: Churches are civil-society bodies and some adherents prefer religious solutions while Etzioni and Galston prefer secular ones.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The platform has schools teach shared values to avoid religious indoctrination, and Etzioni and Galston prefer secular approaches.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Communitarians reject privatising core state functions and see responsive government as a duty.

military-superiority.rationale: Etzioni's Security First favours a muscular foreign policy but superiority over rivals is not a stated aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The platform states that communitarianism is not particularism and treats discrimination as abhorrent; multinational states must protect minorities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Communitarians stress reciprocity and shared membership, not conflict between classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not stated; the emphasis is on reciprocity and responsibility, with positive rights to basic services.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Constitutive communities matter to communitarians and Taylor and Walzer defend group-linked claims, but no stated land position.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not stated; the platform hopes for a global community of democratic communities rather than civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The platform warns against a normless, self-centred, greed-driven society and urges reciprocity over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Etzioni holds strong rights presume strong responsibilities and calls for a declaration of responsibilities; responsive communitarians balance rather than rank them, hence not +2.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No communitarian view on nature's intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Neither the platform nor the SEP discusses population policy, so no stance can be inferred from communitarian principles.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Critique of capitalism's damage to community is not a rejection of industrial civilisation; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Social norms and institutions are valued over disruptive change; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Participation and moral deliberation are prized over automated decision-making; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Etzioni's privacy writings accept limits on privacy for security, which suggests accepting government access.

restore-past-order.rationale: The responsive strand explicitly seeks a new familism and critical evaluation of tradition, not a return to the past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Etzioni sets policy tests of social gains and accountability, but communitarianism is itself a principled stance.

direct-action.rationale: Reform is sought via a Progressive-style social movement and democratic participation, not extra-parliamentary action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Communitarian sources say nothing on whether methods must prefigure ends, so this is left neutral without evidence.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No communitarian source favours abandoning modern society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a communitarian aim; work and saving are honoured.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Reciprocity and contribution are stressed, though basic services are backed as positive rights.

production-for-use.rationale: The sources criticise greed and unchecked capitalism but never propose organising production by need rather than profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Communitarian critics target concentrated economic power, not profit as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with the platform's strong democracy and open participation.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; community ownership is local and voluntary.

taxation-theft.rationale: The platform lists paying taxes as a civic duty and rejects the claim that welfare taxation violates rights; Wikipedia reports this as the critics' claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Rights may be limited when significant common-good gains justify it (Etzioni), and the moral order is not left to private choice.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Communitarians hold that rights depend on communities and that community values are as weighty as freedom, though a core of individual rights is kept.

conscription.rationale: Etzioni proposes greatly expanded national service, and a duty-to-community view supports compulsory service; the scale is inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Participation and voice in responsive democracy are central; membership in communities is not exit-based.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are members of a community with duties, not customers; the platform criticises greed and self-interest.

positive-liberty.rationale: Supporters back positive rights such as education, housing and health care.

media-academia-power.rationale: The platform and SEP make no claim about the political power of universities or media, so this is left neutral.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Discrimination is called abhorrent and Etzioni's tradition accepts the equal standing of persons; no hereditarian claim is part of it.

organic-representation.rationale: Intermediate bodies are prized in civil society, but replacing parties is not the platform; it favours strong democracy.

total-state.rationale: Civil society and intermediate bodies are placed above the state and the state must not harm them.

national-rebirth.rationale: Moral renewal through a social movement is sought, but not radical national rebirth; the platform speaks of a moral deficit.

territorial-expansion.rationale: No communitarian source endorses expansion; the platform emphasises peaceful resolution.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Open participation and responsive democracy are the stated ideal.

bound-labor.rationale: Incompatible with the endorsed rights against discrimination and open participation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Taylor and Sandel say reasoning is embedded in tradition, but communitarians do not hold that all knowledge reflects power.

universal-morality.rationale: SEP describes a minimal universal core of rights (no slavery, torture, genocide) alongside culturally embedded morality, so adherents are split on universal moral truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Communitarians put the common good at the centre but say balance with autonomy depends on context rather than one reasoned good.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a communitarian topic; only the general value of nations as communities of memory could bear on it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Sandel cites Brandeis's industrial democracy approvingly; it is not a platform plank.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; moral schooling is stressed but funding model is not.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The platform criticises demanding more public services without paying for them, but no fiscal doctrine is stated.

economic-freedom.rationale: Etzioni sees concentrated private economic power as the problem, not state limits on markets; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moral voice of communities is stressed, but government by law and democracy remains.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nations are communities of memory, though multinational states are to protect minority rights.

force-without-un.rationale: Etzioni favours muscular moral foreign policy but also stresses national representation in global governance.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Communitarians value tradition, affect and shared values alongside reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigration and welfare-membership are not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The platform stresses work and personal responsibility, and criticises demanding services without contributing; the specific rule is inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Reciprocity and the idea that each member owes something to the rest favour cooperation over opposed classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Communities of memory and inherited traditions are valued as constitutive.

dominated-front.rationale: Not stated; the platform hopes for global democratic community.

workers-nation.rationale: Communitarian sources do not discuss the organisation of the working class, nationally or internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The platform's new familism has both parents involved; authoritarian communitarianism with discrimination against women is distinguished from the responsive strand.

ban-interest.rationale: No communitarian source proposes it; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The platform calls discrimination abhorrent and rejects particularism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is a responsive institution of the community, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Environmental degradation is named as needing national or international action; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Shared values are taught but the platform says its communitarianism is not particularism; immigration is not addressed.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial claims have no place in the sources and the platform rejects particularism.

proportional-representation.rationale: The platform wants more representative and responsive government but names no electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Not stated; the platform hopes for a global community of democratic communities.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; the authoritarian strand is criticised for discrimination against women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The platform seeks to curb private money, special interests and corruption in government.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic measures conflict with rights and the abhorrence of discrimination in the platform.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Etzioni stresses accountability and oversight for policy side effects, but legal liability for past security-force abuses is not discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Communitarians back state support for education, housing, health care and social security, and responsiveness duties.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The platform rejects discrimination and particularism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: A core of universal rights and the platform's rejection of discrimination imply equal rights, though contested at the margins.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Walzer and Taylor defend plural communities, but there is no stated rule.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; open participation and tolerance are stressed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The platform proposes schools teach shared values explicitly to avoid religious indoctrination.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Strong democracy and a government responsive to members are the platform's aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Incompatible with the platform's tolerance, rights against discrimination and minority protections.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Etzioni accepts coercion such as security screening and testing where justified by the common good.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Reciprocity and community are emphasised over struggle and greed.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; Etzioni's security writings accept some limits but party bans are not stated.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Civic republican notions overlap but are not a communitarian doctrine; not addressed.

separated-powers.rationale: Accountability and oversight are stressed in Etzioni's policy tests, but checks and balances are not discussed as such.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed; positive rights to basic services are supported.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Subsidised housing is listed as a positive right, but selling it to tenants is never addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not addressed in the platform; adherents range from pro-union to conservative.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Communitarians focus on social institutions and norms; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The platform affirms tolerance and says communitarianism is not particularism, even as it values shared values.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; elections and participation are the platform's form.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Etzioni allows rights to be limited only for significant common-good gains, with accountability and oversight.

party-controls-media.rationale: Incompatible with an informed public in strong democracy.

party-commands-army.rationale: No communitarian source supports party control of arms; participatory democracy is the rule.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The platform seeks to curb money and corruption in politics but says nothing on legislators' pay levels.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; open deliberation is stressed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Etzioni wants global governance resting on national representation, so adherents are split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; the platform wants community militias and responsive government.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religion is a civil-society institution, with Etzioni and Galston preferring secular approaches.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Duties to the community and nation as community of memory make defeatism incompatible.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Communitarians favour moral voice and more speech rather than censorship (Etzioni on hate speech); inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; accountable, responsive government is stressed.

recall-officials.rationale: Responsiveness and participation, plus curbing corruption, make recall plausible; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Etzioni's muscular foreign policy and global governance suggest engagement; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The platform reads the Second Amendment as community militias, not a replacement of professional forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Local community is valued and New Urbanist design cited, but rural life is not privileged.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nations are valued as communities of memory, but divided-nation questions are not addressed in the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No communitarian source makes claims about the university-educated; Sandel and Etzioni are themselves academics.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Communitarians defend culturally embedded morality but also keep a minimal universal core; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Punishment is not treated as a communitarian topic.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Schools should teach shared values such as tolerance, but sex education is not addressed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Schools should teach shared values without religious indoctrination; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral voice is stressed but pornography law is not stated; adherents are split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; the platform rejects particularism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Multinational states must protect minority political rights; inferred for language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; Taylor and Walzer protect communal practices while the platform values shared law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Communitarians say selves are shaped by unchosen attachments and value shared norms over unrestrained individuality, against Mill.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A state that must grow stronger regardless of democratic limits runs against the stress on empowering civil society and a state that must not harm it.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Markets are criticised for harming communities, but price fixing is never proposed; adherents would split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; its stress on mutual obligation points both ways.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the critique of unregulated markets eroding community, which is not separated from national freedom.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; communitarians value deliberative civic renewal but also inherited institutions and traditions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: the responsive platform pairs strong rights with duties and rejects the authoritarian communitarian strand.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Communitarians stress duties to one's own community, though Etzioni also backs global moral dialogue; the strand is split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; communitarians have no settled view on how the head of state is chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; the platform gives little detailed economic policy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the weight communitarians put on shared history, belonging and attachment to place.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Communitarians hold that rights come with responsibilities and that unregulated capitalism undermines community, so property serves the common good.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the common-good emphasis in the platform, which favours collective protection against harms; not stated on this issue.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from Etzioni's support of global governance and mutual obligations among nations; the sources do not address defence pacts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from respect for the self-determination of communities, though the movement never addressed annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The responsive strand treats religion as a pillar of civil society to keep independent of the state, so it resists state subordination.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the stress on shared identity and common good, which fits a unifying figurehead.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; communitarians value community self-definition but also national cohesion, so adherents split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The platform stresses localism, diversity and decentralised communities, which fits regions keeping their own arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The responsive platform is democratic and pluralist, so a sacred ruler of divine descent is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the platform's support of state-backed social rights and shared burdens, which leans toward progressive rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: Communitarians hold that people are shaped by families, communities and schools, though they allow some innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The platform ties rights to responsibilities and democratic accountability, so rulers above the law are rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; communitarian concern with community and Earth-bound problems pulls against space as a central goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from pluralist civil-society thinking; the sources do not discuss mixed government.

leader-cult.rationale: The platform stresses democratic participation and shared responsibilities, which opposes glorifying a leader.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from Etzioni's emphasis on strong families and parental responsibility for both parents; custody law is not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from the platform's centrist, pluralist stance and focus on shared moral culture over class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; communitarians stress local community ties, which is split between protecting those on the land and protecting property.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by the platform or the SEP; communities' claims on homes cut both ways.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from Etzioni's pluralist, responsive form, which rejects aggressive nationalism, though the SEP notes some communitarians defend national belonging.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Responsive communitarians affirm core individual rights and civil liberties, so penalties for leaving a religion are inferred to conflict with them.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the platform's commitment to individual rights and liberties within community.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; communitarians value local community, but nothing in the sources sets a view on monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the responsive form's pluralism and respect for rights, which does not extend to ethnic political unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The SEP links communitarianism to protecting the cultures of communities, and the platform values diversity, but the responsive form stresses shared common values.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the platform's balance of diversity with shared civic commitments, which favors integration into the country where people live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The platform stresses moral voices, shared values and culture as shaping society, so communitarians doubt that economic conditions alone drive change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the critique of unregulated markets and concentrated power, though not a topic of the platform.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; the critique of unregulated markets and the concern for fairness to ordinary taxpayers cut against each other.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Responsive communitarians seek to balance majority decision with rights and the SEP records worries about majorities, so courts' role is accepted; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between equal representation as a social right and distrust of quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the stress on interdependent communities and the SEP's criticism of nationalism as closure.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on rights balanced by responsibilities and its concern with regulating markets that erode community.

moral-incentives.rationale: Etzioni calls for national service and a sense of duty, but the platform does not propose replacing pay as the main incentive.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The responsive form is centrist and democratic and its platform stresses civic participation; inferred rejection of armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on equal civic membership and shared responsibilities, which is hard to square with rank by birth.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Communitarians stress shared traditions and shared-values schooling, which supports teaching a nation's own history at the centre, though responsive communitarians also want diversity within unity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: responsive communitarianism values the integrity of each community and its traditions, which cuts against imperial tutelage, though nothing in the sources addresses it.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Responsive Communitarian Platform and Etzioni call for schools to teach shared civic values and responsibilities, and national service, which supports civic loyalty, though not unconditional pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed by the platform; Etzioni is centrist on diversity and adherents split between group-conscious and colour-blind approaches.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary mechanics are not addressed by communitarians; the movement criticises unregulated markets but gives no view on who should create money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: communitarians criticise markets for eroding community but seek to balance and regulate them, not to replace them, so they expect reformed capitalism to persist.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: responsive communitarians are wary of nationalist assertion and stress mutual responsibility among communities, though nothing addresses imperial legacies directly.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: the platform favours moderated, localist but not autarkic economics, and no source endorses breaking ties with rich countries.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: this is a Marxist claim outside communitarian thought, which sees workers as members of communities and not as beneficiaries of imperial extraction.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Communitarians put common-good duties ahead of unrestricted individual rights, and Etzioni stresses balancing rights and responsibilities, so unlimited freedom to refuse service is unlikely to be endorsed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The platform embraces rights, while insisting on matching responsibilities; adherents accept constitutionally protected rights, though philosophical communitarians criticise rights-centred politics.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed as a defining issue; adherents are split between self-determination arguments and respect for settled agreements and borders, so the answer is inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rule by election rather than inheritance follows from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

minority-veto.rationale: A near-universal individual veto is not a position of the mainstream; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The right to resist rulers who break the law and abuse their trust is inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities, applied to the question of who holds supreme lawmaking authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not a defining issue; a welfare-limited use of animals is inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities, applied to whether the privileged owe a duty to the less fortunate.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Rejecting withdrawal from public affairs is inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: This is a critical-theory claim rather than a position of the ideology; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A hegemony account of class power is not part of the ideology; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency-style explanations of poverty are rejected or not held; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices by birth conflicts with the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties; the answer is a loose inference from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities favouring national autonomy.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The statement excludes foreign trade, loans and investment; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist territorial claims conflict with the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Hereditary or descent-based political leadership conflicts with the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities applied to constitutional founding values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Condemning both fascism and communism as totalitarian is inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The historical consensus is that slavery was the main cause; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Adherents are split between preserving history and removing honours; the ideology gives no settled position beyond the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities applied to public programmes for disadvantaged groups.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection of victims is inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Whether institutions are universal or civilization-specific is inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for the military conflicts with the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the communitarian emphasis on community, civil society and balancing rights with responsibilities applied to recognising and paying domestic labour.

missingStatements.text: Individual rights should come with matching legal or civic responsibilities, such as jury service, paying taxes and national service.
missingStatements.rationale: The platform and Etzioni insist that strong rights presume strong responsibilities and call for a declaration of responsibilities.

missingStatements.text: Parents who bring children into the world have a moral duty to give them moral education and character formation, not only material support.
missingStatements.rationale: The platform states that bringing children into the world entails a moral responsibility and treats the family as the first line of moral education.

missingStatements.text: Public life should be shaped by a shared community moral culture, not left to individual choice alone.
missingStatements.rationale: The platform speaks of communities as rich resources of moral voices and warns of a normless, self-centred society.

missingStatements.text: Divorce laws should be changed to signal society's concern for the children involved, making divorce harder.
missingStatements.rationale: The platform treats widespread divorce as a sign of social trouble and proposes changing divorce laws, while the SEP notes support for making divorce harder.

notes: Responsive (Etzioni) communitarianism is centrist; communitarian philosophers (Sandel, MacIntyre) lean more anti-liberal and traditionalist, and authoritarian communitarianism would answer hierarchy, order and speech questions very differently. The Education Week report was opened and informs s4 alongside the CS Monitor review.
